'''Brett Helgeson Welcome to Mos Eisley''' is a [[Light]] constructed list published on Decipher Deck Designs.

== Deck info ==
* '''Player:''' [[Brett Helgeson]]
* '''Published:''' December 1997 (Decipher Deck Designs)
* '''Format:''' [[Premiere - Cloud City]]
* '''Side:''' [[Light]]
* '''Starting Card:''' {{CardLink|Tatooine: Mos Eisley|Premiere-L-tatooinemoseisley.gif}}
* '''Strategy:''' Welcome to Mos Eisley
* '''GEMP Importable deck:''' [[Media:PCC Welcome to Mos Eisley Helgeson LS.txt |Download]]

== Introduction ==

This is a very, very unpredictable design. I doubt if even Han would want to wager on the outcome! However, when it works, you will utterly anihilate your opponent. But when things go bad . . .

The whole premise of this deck is to make the Imperials do all the work - while you sit and drain away. It uses two (2) whole sites, and a fair amount of interupts and effects to generate force, while giving you some obscenly high destiny draws. (The average of this deck is around 3.1!).

== Strategy ==

The whole idea behind this deck is to make the imperials come and fight you on your terms. Use Spaceport Speeders in conjunction with all the ground vehicles to generate as much force as possible. The Crash site memorial is there as a 'battery' - to recharge your force when you need it. I included Figrin D'an as a backup in case the Memorial gets altered away - with your high destiny, you should win every wager.

There are a few spies to help with protecting drains, but just incase your spy gets killed, plenty of Nabrun Lieds to jump around with. Because of the high destiny, you should be getting around 9 force everytime you sell Luke's speeder, and 6 with any other. Its possible to get as much as 19 force from the landspeeder! Try to sell as much as you can as early as you can in the game - before the Imperials can get anyone out to sense those Speeders! I tossed in a grappling hook as a way to limit the number of senses your opponent can throw at you.

As you can see, there are no senses or alters - which might be a problem. I included "It could be Worse" as an easy way to deal with force drains - just spend the force from each drain, saving your life force as much as possible. Use Traffic Control to put back excess speeders - and remember to count where they are - drawing a couple of sixes (esp. with "The force is strong with this one" and I've got a bad feeling about this) can really spank your opponent. Like I said to begin with - this deck either WORKS, or you're left out in the cold. Give it a shot and tell me what might be good to include/throw out.
